title: Add Two Numbers
description: You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. The digits are stored in reverse order, and each node contains a single digit. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a reverse-ordered linked list.
input_format: First line contains `n1` followed by digits. Second line contains `n2` followed by digits.
output_format: Space-separated result digits in reverse order.
hints: Traverse both lists node by node, simulating column addition.
Keep track of the carry (`carry = sum // 10`) at each step.
Create a new node with `sum % 10` for each position.

starter_code.python:

reference_solution:
import sys
lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
if len(lines) >= 2:
    p1 = lines[0].split()
    p2 = lines[1].split()
    d1 = [int(x) for x in p1[1:1+int(p1[0])]]
    d2 = [int(x) for x in p2[1:1+int(p2[0])]]
    carry = 0
    res = []
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(d1) or j < len(d2) or carry:
        v1 = d1[i] if i < len(d1) else 0
        v2 = d2[j] if j < len(d2) else 0
        s = v1 + v2 + carry
        carry = s // 10
        res.append(s % 10)
        i += 1; j += 1
    print(' '.join(map(str, res)))
